question: Human trafficking and human rights violations through recruitment of nonRussian nationals, in particular from Africa, for Russia’s war of aggression in Ukraine

In its illegal war of aggression against Ukraine, Russia is employing deceptive tactics and coercion to recruit thousands of foreign nationals from African states. Recruited under false promises of employment, education and citizenship and then stripped of their identity documents, they are forced to serve at the frontline in Ukraine, where they are often used as mere cannon fodder.

Recruited women are tricked into working in factories under dangerous and exploitative conditions. These recruitment schemes are enabled through state-linked (paramilitary) companies, intermediaries, military structures and embassy officials. Parliament has called for the EU and the Member States to support efforts to tackle human trafficking, impose targeted sanctions and facilitate release and repatriation.
Recently, the United Kingdom has imposed targeted sanctions to counter these illicit recruitment schemes. 1.

What concrete measures are the Commission and the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (VP/HR) undertaking to dismantle illicit recruitment networks, combat human trafficking and address the Russian disinformation practices that enable it?
Is the Commission or the VP/HR initiating, or considering initiating, targeted sanctions similar to those imposed by the United Kingdom?

What specific measures are the Commission or the VP/HR taking, or planning to take, to ensure the repatriation of trafficked individuals, and what financial and operational support will be made available to that end?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.8.2026) The EU strongly condemns Russia’s deceitful and coercive recruitment of third country citizens, including Africans, to fight in its war against Ukraine and to work in its military industry.

The High Representative/Vice-President and EU representatives have raised this issue in diplomatic and political contacts with countries affected and have invited them to warn their citizens against this threat, against signing up for job or training opportunities in Russia.

Furthermore, the European External Action Service has been raising awareness on this issue through public diplomacy and strategic communication campaigns, including through the network of EU Delegations, notably in Africa.

The High Representative/Vice-President has also discussed with the leadership of Ukraine possible specific measures to be implemented, given the varying circumstances of the foreign national individuals in question. Any additional restrictive measures on individuals and entities are decided by the Council by unanimity.
